hadith_en: Narrated A'ishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ that a Jewish woman came to beg from her and said, "may Allah give you refuge from the punishment of the grave." A'ishah, upon hearing this, asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ:"Are people punished in their graves?", The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took refuge in Allah from that. Then, one morning the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out on a journey and there was an eclipse of the sun, and he returned in the late morning and passed between the rear of the dwellings. Then he stood and prayed, and the people stood behind him. He stood for a long time, and then went into bowing for a long time. Then he rose and stood for a long time, though less than the first time, and then went into bowing for a long time, though less than the first time. Then he rose and went down into prostration. Then he stood for a long time, though less than the time before, and then went into bowing for a long time, though less than the time before. Then he rose and stood for a long time, though less than the time before, and then went into bowing for a long time, though less than the time before. Then he rose and went down into prostration. When he had finished, he ﷺ said what Allah willed him to say, and then he told them to seek protection for themselves from the punishment of the grave.".
syarah_en: The punishment and bliss of the grave are true and real, and we have been commanded to seek protection from its torment. One of the occasions on which we should seek protection from it is when the signs [of the Hour] occur, namely the lunar and solar eclipse. During those times, there are signs and lessons on the Absolute Divine Power of Allah [that can be observed].  Hence, the sun and moon are two signs from among the creations of Allah - May He be Exalted - establishing His Majesty; and that they are subjected to His Power and Might.  The Prophet ﷺtaught us what we [should] do when this phenomenon occurs.In this hadeeth, a Jewish woman came to see ʿA’ishah(may Allah be pleased with her), asking for something that she had given her. When she gave it to her, the Jewess supplicated for her - and perhaps that was a way of showing appreciation for what she had given her - and said: ‘May Allah give you refuge from the torment of the grave.’ It has been said that she came inquiring about the punishment of the grave and invoked Allah to protect her from it, like what [is mentioned] in a narration from al-Bayhaqi in the book: Proving The Punishment of the Grave [i.e. KitaabIthbaatʿAdhaab al-Qabr] : “A Jewish woman came to see ʿA’ishah(may Allah be pleased with her) and said: “Have you heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentions anything about the torment of the grave?”ʿA’ishah(may Allah be pleased with her) said to the Prophet ﷺ, inquiring about the statement of the Jewess: ‘Do the people suffer pain in their graves?’  Then, The Prophet ﷺ sought refuge in Allah from the torments of the grave [i.e., by saying AʿoodhubilLaah- “I seek refuge in Allah” and the like].  And he ﷺ confirmed the words of the Jewess regarding the torment of the grave; and the evident questioning of ʿA’ishah(may Allah be pleased with her) indicates that she did not know about the torments of the grave before that moment.  But rather, she knew [about] the rewards and punishments [of the grave] after the resurrection.  Perhaps the knowledge of the Jewish woman about the suffering in the grave was from what she heard about it from the Torah or in one of their books [i.e., other religious books in the Jewish canon].Then, the Prophet ﷺ rode out one morning, during which the sun eclipsed.  The eclipse of the sun [occurs when] its light disappears in the sky.  For the most part, the solar eclipse is expressed by [the Arabic word]: al-kusoof, and the lunar eclipse as al-khusoof. [However,] these two words may be used [interchangeably] to express one another as well - and this is what occurred in this narration.The Prophet ﷺ returned during the forenoon, and he passed between the rear of the dwellings, i.e., between the living quarters of his wives (may Allah be pleased with them).  Then, he ﷺ stood to perform the Eclipse prayer, and completed two units. After he commenced the prayer, he stoodin the first prayer unit for a long time, wherein he ﷺ recited [more ayaat from the Quran] after al-Fatihah, for approximately the amount of time it would take one to recite Surah al-Baqarah - as it is [related] in another hadeeth narrated by Ibn Abbaas(may Allah be pleased with them) in Saheeh al-Bukhaaree and Saheeh Muslim.In another report in Saheeh al-Bukhaaree and Saheeh Muslim [narrated] on the authority of ʿA’ishah(may Allah be pleased with her), she related that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited aloud during the eclipse prayer.Then, the Prophet ﷺ bowed and prolonged it.  Thereafter, he rose from bowing [and stood] a long time - however it was shorter than the first standing. Thereafter, he ﷺ performed a second bowing, however it was less in duration than the first bowing.  After he ﷺ rose from bowing, straightening up into a standing position [before] proceeding to perform two prostrations.  Next, he stood up to perform the second unit; thus, he ﷺ performed it like [how] it was performed in the first prayer unit; except he shortened the time of all its actions; where he performed: a long standing, yet shorter than the first; a lengthened bowing yetshorter than the first.  Then, he ﷺrose, straightening himself from bowing and stood [before] continuing to perform another bowing, yet both were shorter in length than the first bowing and standing. Subsequently, he ﷺ prostrated twice, and after, he sat so that he could perform the tashahhud and tasleem.After, he ﷺ stood up to deliver a sermon to the people; and said whatever Allah wished for him to say.  Thereafter, he ordered the people to seek protection from the torments of the grave.  The meaning of ‘seeking protection from the punishments of the grave is: [that we] sincerely seek refuge in Allah from the agonies of the grave, because He is the only One in whose hands lie preservation and protection.It is mentioned in a report [narrated] by al-Bukhaaree, on the authority of ʿA’ishah(may Allah be pleased with her) who narrates that he ﷺ stood up to deliver a sermon after finishing the prayer.  Then, he praised and extolled Allah, and mentioned that the sun and moon are two signs [of many which have been created by] Allah, and they do not eclipse because of the death or birth of anyone.This serves as a response to what some people surmised: [i.e.] that the solar eclipse happened because of the passing of Ibraheem, the son of the Prophet ﷺ.  Then he ﷺ enjoined the invocation of Allah, Exalted be He, with: the performance of the takbeer, prayer, and giving charity upon seeing the eclipse.  He ﷺ then warned them of the indecencies of adultery and fornication, and alarmed the people of the retribution of Allah, The Mighty and Majestic.Some of the other benefits that we can conclude from this hadeeth is to bear in mind and know that the torments of the grave are a reality, and that it is not specific to this nation.We should be careful when reading or discussing about the narration[s] as attested by the People of the Book; and to strive and see if their account is compatible with the Book of Allah or the statements of His Messenger ﷺ.  For that reason, we should refrain from reporting them until we know whether it is truth or falsehood.Lastly, we learn from this hadeeth that we should seek refuge in Allah concerning the punishments of the grave following the completion of prayer because it is a time where supplications and invocations are answered..
